request: Determine all schematic wire manipulation/modification use cases and code updates using Altium Designer as a behavioral template.
status: Audit complete; proposed behavior/code changes are not implemented or ratified by this record.
scope: 54 documented/reference Altium and ordinary manipulation cases cross-checked against 43 Datum source cases. Reference unknowns and optional features are explicit; this is not exhaustive installed-Altium or Datum runtime qualification.
owner_observations: Attempted junction drag moved an R1-C1 wire body and detached fixed pins.
Original R1-C1 source wire was unsplit; redrawing endpoint-connected C1/Q1/R1 geometry behaved as expected.
Owner expects editable wire ends and nearest-pin snapping.
conclusions: The original T is electrically connected. Missing editing ownership makes equivalent unsplit and segmented drawings behave differently.
The central update is a shared source-qualified wire edit basis and canonical handle/attachment plan, followed by acquisition and snap integration.
Automatic source splitting alone is not a complete or harmless fix; crossing-junction deletion, raw identity and Bus Entry references must remain deliberate.
Current exact pin snapping during creation exists; nearest-candidate ranking and electrical snap integration in Move are the gaps.
Altium is a behavioral comparator. Datum shared tooling, complete-operation lock refusal, canonical journal, explicit crossing and selection key laws remain controlling.

altium_cases.behavior: Place Wire or Ctrl+W starts wiring; click/Enter anchors the start and subsequent vertices.
First Esc/right-click completes the current wire; a subsequent one exits repeated placement.
Backspace/Delete removes the latest placed vertex during wiring.
Esc/right-click escapes the current interactive stage or command.
altium_cases.limit: Exact mouse-held cancellation event phases and atomicity are not specified.

altium_cases.behavior: Selected-wire endpoint handles reposition individual ends.
Dragging a vertex keeps wire endpoints anchored.
Dragging a selected segment keeps other vertices and endpoints anchored.
Holding and moving an unselected wire repositions the entire wire.
altium_cases.limit: Literal object-movement description; actual connectivity behavior depends on Always Drag. No default setting is established.

altium_cases.behavior: Hold a selected segment and press Insert to add a vertex.
Hold an existing vertex and press Delete to remove it.
Endpoint repositioning supports changing length; no separate current Extend Wire command established.
Properties exposes editable vertex coordinates and add/remove controls.
Manual modes include 45-degree, 90-degree and unrestricted angles.
Shift+Space cycles wire placement modes; Space switches start/end corner orientation in orthogonal modes.
Auto Wire offers point-to-point path calculation with obstacle avoidance.
Move ignores connectivity; Drag attempts to retain it.
Move Selection ignores connections; Drag Selection retains electrical connections.
Always Drag retains wiring while moving components or component selections.
Ctrl temporarily reverses Always Drag behavior.
Moving a union member can move the group; electrical dragging can override union movement.
Drag Orthogonal keeps connected wiring orthogonal; disabling it permits oblique adjustment.
Current pages disagree on Space versus Ctrl+Space for connected-wire corner modes.
altium_cases.limit: Preferences and shortcut reference assign Ctrl+Space; editing overview assigns Space and assigns Ctrl+Space to selection rotation. Verify against a target installation.

altium_cases.behavior: Electrical snapping overrides the placement grid within its attraction range, permitting off-grid connections.
Grid settings are document-specific; Shift+E toggles electrical hotspot snapping.
Attraction-range snapping is documented; nearest-candidate metric, ambiguity resolution and equal-distance pin priority are not specified.
Break Wires At Autojunctions enabled splits existing T-contact segments; disabled leaves through-wires unbroken.
Compiler-generated junctions are automatic, not independently graphically editable.
Removing one T branch removes its redundant junction and merges the remaining two segments.
Selected wire segments can be individually subselected and deleted.
Break Wire removes a visible cut length; modes target a segment, grid multiple or fixed length.
Break Wire repeats until Esc/right-click exits.
Break Wire removes material; autojunction splitting is separately configured.
altium_cases.limit: Do not equate a gap-producing cutter with connectivity-preserving T segmentation.

altium_cases.behavior: Optimize Wires & Buses removes overlapping wire/polyline/bus redundancy.
Components Cut Wires terminates cut segments on two hot pins; optimization must also be enabled.
With cross-junction conversion disabled, newly crossing wires remain disconnected; conversion produces adjacent three-way junctions.
Protect Locked Objects prevents movement and excludes locked members from moved selections; disabling protection prompts a warning.
Select objects, inspect common properties, then apply edits through shared panels.
Aligned parallel multiwire endpoint extension was not established in the reviewed current Designer pages.
altium_cases.limit: Search surfaced CircuitStudio descriptions; these were deliberately excluded as evidence for Designer.

altium_cases.behavior: Ctrl+Z undoes; Ctrl+Y redoes.
The tutorial deletes a wire, undoes the deletion, and revalidates connectivity.
Document Save writes the active document; project-only Save does not save constituent design documents. Save All covers modified files.
Local Save updates the working copy; Save to Server separately commits selected project changes to the Workspace.
Closing projects/application with multiple unsaved documents offers save/discard choices according to local/Workspace state.
When enabled, Local History retains the previous file version on each save; autosaved versions can be included.
Cold-reopen undo persistence and exact per-wire gesture transaction grouping were not established by these sources.
altium_cases.limit: Local History snapshots are not evidence of a persistent Undo stack.
